editorial:
Imagine being the school outcast and finally having a way to get back at the popular kids who make your life a nightmare. That is exactly where you find yourself with Faye, a teen witch who decides to call on a dark version of Cupid to handle her bullies. Instead of love and arrows, this version of Cupid brings total chaos and a lot of blood. The vibe is like a mean-girls drama mixed with a scary slasher movie, making it a wild ride that turns a romantic holiday into a complete bloodbath for the students.

You will probably love how the movie keeps things moving quickly without getting bogged down. The acting feels natural for a teen horror flick, and the kills are creative enough to keep you interested. While some of the special effects look a bit cheap, it adds to the campy fun of the whole thing.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, the students realize that the only way to stop the killing spree is to break the spell Faye cast. After a lot of screaming and running, Faye has to face the consequences of her anger. She manages to reverse the ritual just in time, sending the evil Cupid back to where he came from. The movie wraps up with the survivors shaken and the bullies finally learning that being mean has a very high price.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen slashers and dark twists on holidays.
